headline: High prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Roo Code’s filesystem/browser/MCP access paired with Taipy’s data-ops workflows; shared workspace and unverified interaction raise cascading-error concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code can read/write the VS Code workspace, run browsers, and use MCP; its state is shared via filesystem. Taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool, so if its outputs or files are fed into Roo Code, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF Taipy-generated files or UI text are opened in Roo Code without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF both agents share a workspace directory, Roo Code can ingest attacker-controlled content from Taipy outputs.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Taipy outputs into Roo Code prompts.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Add a manual review step before copying Taipy text into Roo Code.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, provenance-tagged sources.
requires-engineering: add content provenance labels to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code touches source code and browser screenshots, has broad network egress, and handles model-provider API keys. Taipy is open-source and network-egress-free, so the main leakage path is Roo Code exporting shared workspace contents or screenshots; Taipy itself is not a transmission risk. The shared filesystem makes leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared VS Code workspace, Roo Code can read them.
IF Roo Code sends workspace context or screenshots to its model API, those contents may leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared workspace.
Use a separate repo for sensitive data.
Turn off browser/screenshot capture when not needed.
Limit Roo Code API keys to least-privilege accounts.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad network egress; its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. Taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool that may also mutate shared project artifacts. Without locking or coordination in either profile, concurrent writes to the same workspace or git state can conflict and corrupt work.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF both agents modify the same git branch without locks, history conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Serialize git commits through one operator.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
Pause one agent while the other writes shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional workspace coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can generate code, browser-derived content, and tool actions; Taipy is automation-oriented and may consume upstream artifacts. If Taipy treats Roo Code output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream data workflows. The interaction is inferred rather than documented, so medium is appropriate with uncertainty escalated from the shared-workspace pathway.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes Roo Code-generated files or instructions without verification, mistakes propagate.
IF Roo Code produces code or configs that Taipy executes, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of Roo Code outputs before Taipy uses them.
Validate generated files with tests or schema checks.
Keep Taipy execution inputs read-only until approved.
Log provenance for every handoff between agents.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Roo Code handles browser screenshots and source code and may send context to configured model APIs; Taipy’s profile shows no touched data classes or network egress. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance gap is evident from Roo Code’s broader external-data exposure. Taipy is not cited for a mismatch because its profile lacks relevant compliance fields.
conditions: IF browser screenshots contain regulated data and Roo Code sends them to an external model API, compliance obligations may apply.
IF Taipy is used with regulated datasets but lacks documented retention controls, policy gaps may emerge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in browser screenshots.
Use a local or approved model endpoint for Roo Code.
Document retention settings for any shared artifacts.
Separate regulated datasets from development workspaces.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls.
